faq.q: What makes Arabic mehndi different from Indian mehndi?
faq.a: Arabic mehndi uses bold floral patterns with significant negative space, while Indian designs feature dense, full-coverage patterns with paisleys and fine detail.

faq.q: Is Arabic mehndi good for beginners?
faq.a: Yes, Arabic mehndi is considered the best starting style for beginners. The flowing, larger patterns are more forgiving than intricate Indian designs.

faq.q: How dark does Arabic mehndi stain?
faq.a: On palms and fingertips, Arabic mehndi stains a deep reddish-brown. On the back of the hand, expect a lighter orange-brown.

faq.q: How long should I leave the mehndi paste on?
faq.a: Keep the paste on for at least four to six hours. Many people leave it overnight for a darker stain.

faq.q: Why does my mehndi look orange at first?
faq.a: Fresh henna stains are orange. The colour deepens to reddish brown over the next 24 to 48 hours as the dye oxidises.

faq.q: Is black henna safe?
faq.a: Natural henna is never black. Products sold as black henna often contain PPD, a hair-dye chemical that can cause skin reactions, so they are best avoided.
